overview: A two-page telegram from the U.S. legation in Bern reports a German press account, originating in Tokyo, of Japan’s wartime program for prospecting, mining, smelting, and processing rare minerals. It identifies sources of zirconium and other strategic elements across Japan’s empire and the wider East Asian sphere, describes Korea as the principal source, and names several Japanese companies involved in mining, refining, research, and industrial organization.

people.name: Leland Harrison
people.role: U.S. diplomatic representative in Bern and sender of the telegram

people.name: Lieutenant General Tada
people.role: Director of the Scientific Mobilization Organization

subfiles.title: Telegram from Harrison in Bern on Japanese rare-mineral production
subfiles.about: Reports a German press account of Japanese wartime research, extraction, and industrial processing of rare minerals throughout Japan’s East Asian sphere.
subfiles.summary: Harrison relays a German press report from Tokyo stating that Japan had undertaken special research into prospecting, smelting, and processing rare minerals for war industries. The report lists zirconium, tantalum, lithium, beryllium, neodymium, caesium, titanium, and niobium as available in East Asia and identifies Korea as the principal source of rare minerals. It also describes the roles of the Nippon Seiko Company, Nippon Zirconium Company, Nippon Rare Minerals Company, Rare Metals Refining Company, and the newly founded Nippon Rare Elements Company in mining, research, refining, and industrial coordination.

interest: The telegram offers a compact Allied intelligence snapshot of Japan’s efforts to secure specialized metals essential to advanced wartime manufacturing. It is especially useful for tracing the geographical reach of Japanese resource extraction—from Korea and Taiwan to Burma, Malaya, Indochina, Mongolia, and Manchuria—and for identifying firms participating in the rare-metals sector. Its transmission through Bern and reliance on a German press report also illustrate the indirect channels through which wartime economic intelligence circulated.
